current.text: He plays for Miami after a trade from Milwaukee.

Miami lacks point guards and ball handlers. He played basically as a point guard in Miami's first preseason game. It is an open question whether Miami starts a traditional point guard or lets him run point.
Experts expect 32 to 33 minutes a game in Miami and over 60 games, but not 70 games.
With few other creators in Miami, he should keep high usage and his assist rate should rise.
His fantasy value probably rises after the trade. The extra minutes may offset the usual first-year adjustment on a new team.
With more minutes and aggression, his FG% could get back to about 65%.
Experts call him a clear number 5 pick in category leagues. He should not fall past pick 5, and getting him at pick 6 or 7 is value.
Experts call his ESPN category rank of about 20 egregious and say he is at worst 9th.
In an auction mock he went for 58 USD. The expert expected about 60 USD and thinks that is about where he should sit.
At least 15 of his missed games last season came while Milwaukee was tanking.
Experts are not very worried about last season's calf injuries, but a new calf issue would be a concern.
Nothing indicates he will sit back-to-backs. He may sit one or two.
Miami has the league-minimum 13 back-to-backs and none in the fantasy playoffs.
With the March 28 end, Miami has a weak 4-3-3 schedule in our playoff weeks, 10 games in total.
Miami's depth is poor, so the team relies heavily on him. The East is stacked, so Miami may not be able to rest players for long stretches.

durable.text: He has excellent FG% on high volume and is among the league leaders in FG% impact.
He is a bad free throw shooter on high volume, with the worst FT% impact in the league. He will probably stay bad, though a random 70% season would not be crazy.
His points and rebounds are far above the league pool. He is a double-digit rebounder and gives guard-like assists for a forward.
He makes few threes and is not a good shooter. Threes are easy to make up elsewhere.
His steals and blocks have declined from his peak, and it is not clear they will come back.
He has a long injury history, with persistent knee problems and calf injuries last season. Experts also list his age as a concern.
Plain nine-cat and roto rankings undervalue him because of his free throws. His real impact in H2H is huge.

Experts agree a punt FT% build is the natural fit, but they differ on how strict it must be. Some say drafting him means punting FT%. Another says you should not chase free throws around him but can still be decent in the category.

note: Experts treat him as a clear number 5 pick in H2H categories. Prices sit around 58 to 64 USD (Yahoo average cost 62, ESPN 64.3, 62 USD in our league last season, 58 USD in a mock), so plan to pay about 60 USD and build punt FT% around his FG%, points, rebounds and assists. Early in the season, check that he gets the expected 32 to 33 minutes, whether he runs point for Miami, and whether any new calf issue shows up. Also remember Miami has a weak 4-3-3 schedule in our playoff weeks.
